how_body.every_question_runs_through: Every question runs through a fixed pipeline. The decision to answer or refuse is deterministic and never depends on a live model call, so the system behaves the same with or without an LLM. Each stage below records a status and a timing. After you ask, the
how_body.grounding_is_decided_in: Grounding is decided in two layers. First, a deterministic embedding similarity between each claim and its cited source must clear a threshold. This is authoritative and reproducible. Second, when a live provider is configured, a separate, cheaper model is shown only the claim and its cited source and asked, strictly, whether the source supports the claim. It returns JSON:
how_body.shows_the_real_run: shows the real run, and every step there is clickable for the detail of what happened, including the LLM judge's verdict on each claim.
how_body.the_judge_is_corroboration: . The judge is corroboration, recorded in the trace, never the deciding vote. So a flaky model can never turn a refusal into an answer. Open the grounding step in the trace to read the judge's verdict and reasoning for each claim.

reason.claim_ungrounded: A statement in the draft answer was not sufficiently supported by its cited source.
reason.combination_forbidden: The sources say these must not be used together, so there is no safe combined dose to give.
reason.dose_unsupported: The draft answer contained a dose that no source about this medicine states.
reason.fallback: The pipeline could not produce a fully grounded answer, so it declined.
reason.form_unsupported: The question names a form or route that no source about this medicine describes.
reason.input_blocked: The query was stopped by an input guard before reaching the pipeline.
reason.insufficient_context: The retrieved sources did not contain enough to answer safely.
reason.limit_not_stated: The sources give a dose but no limit, so they can't answer a question about a maximum or minimum.
reason.no_relevant_source: No document was similar enough to the question to be trustworthy, so the system refused before generating anything.
reason.patient_unsafe: The answer from the sources doesn't fit the patient you described. The check above names the rule.
reason.population_not_covered: The question is about a patient group the sources don't cover, so an answer written for adults could be unsafe.
reason.proposal_unverifiable: A regimen in the question could not be checked part by part against the sources, so it was refused rather than guessed at.
reason.rate_limited: Too many requests in a short window. This protects the live service.
reason.source_conflict: Two approved documents give different doses of the same medicine, so no single dose can be given until a reviewer resolves the conflict.
reason.stated_value_unsupported: The question states a value that no trusted source supports, so confirming it could be unsafe.
reason.term_not_covered: The question names something the trusted sources never mention, so there is nothing to ground an answer on.
reason.unsupported_language: The question is in a language this installation cannot check against its sources, so it was refused rather than answered from English text by accident.

srv.explain.decision: The gate. Refuse if any input guard blocked, the retrieval gate failed, coverage failed, the model had insufficient context, any claim is ungrounded, or the dosage guard failed. A refusal is put in the review queue when one is running, and the answer says whether it was; the reason is also given as a stable code. Otherwise answer, assembling the grounded claims into prose with bracketed citations.
srv.explain.dosage_guard: The showpiece check, and deterministic: every value with a clinical unit in the answer (for example '15 mg') must be stated by a retrieved source about the medicine it is attributed to. Numbers and units are compared, so '15 mg' and 'fifteen milligrams' match and '15 mcg' does not. Otherwise the system refuses and names the offending value.
srv.explain.generate: The question and the retrieved sources are sent to the LLM, which must return structured JSON: a list of claims, each citing the source ids it came from. With no API key, an extractive fallback picks up to three sentences from the passages about the topic, scored on meaning, on the question's own words and on whether the passage is the kind of section that answers it (dose, side effects, symptoms...), and gives each part of a two-part question its own sentence. Either way the output is the same shape and passes through the same guards.
srv.explain.grounding_check: For every claim, a deterministic embedding similarity is computed between the claim and its cited source. The claim must cite a real source and clear the grounding threshold, and a sentence that names no medicine must belong to the passage it cites: every name and clinical term in it has to be in that passage. Each claim also records how relevant it is to the question and where in the passage it sits, for information only. When a live LLM is configured, a second, cheaper model acts as a judge and is asked, strictly, whether the source supports the claim. The deterministic result is authoritative; the judge is recorded as corroboration so the demo stays reproducible.
srv.explain.patient_checks: When the question is about a specific patient, the formulary's rules for every medicine named are applied to that patient: allergies, conditions, interactions with current medicines, age, weight, kidney and liver function, pregnancy, lab results and high-alert status. A problem that makes the answer unsafe refuses it; others are shown as warnings.
srv.explain.pii_redaction: Before anything is logged, embedded, or sent to a model, identifiers are replaced with placeholders such as [NAME] and [DATE]. Each detector proposes spans with a score; checksums (NHS mod-11, Luhn for cards and provider numbers, mod-97 for IBANs, social security rules) and real calendar dates confirm them, and nearby cue words ('patient', 'husband', 'DOB') raise or lower the score. Names come from titles, relation and role cues, 'SURNAME, Given', and a bundled list of given names; words the documents know, medicine names and months are never names, and a dose or an age under 90 is never removed. If spaCy or Presidio is installed it can add people and places. Ages over 89 become 90. This is a safety net, not a guarantee.
srv.explain.proposal_check: When the question proposes a regimen ('Is 15 mg twice a day okay for X?'), its dose, frequency, route, duration, daily maximum and timing are read out and compared, part by part, with what the sources say about that medicine. Any difference gives a 'No' that names both; every part matching gives a 'Yes'; a part that cannot be read or checked (no unit, an unknown or second medicine, a source that contradicts itself) refuses the question rather than guessing. No model is involved.
srv.explain.rate_limit: A simple in-memory limiter caps requests per minute per process, so a burst of traffic cannot overwhelm the service.
srv.explain.remembered_answer: An identical question, with no patient details, asked again while the earlier answer was still current and the sources had not changed. The earlier run's checks are shown unchanged, and this request has its own audit record.
srv.explain.retrieval_gate: If even the best passage scores below the retrieval threshold, the system refuses now, before any text is generated. The cheapest refusal happens before a model is ever called.
srv.explain.retrieve: The query is embedded with a sentence-transformer and compared against every document vector in the vector store, alongside a keyword search. The top-k passages are returned with cosine similarity scores.
srv.explain.schema_validate: The model output is parsed and validated against a strict Pydantic schema. Malformed output is retried once, then falls back to extractive. Free-text answers are never accepted.
srv.explain.scope_check: Rejects empty or over-long queries and obvious prompt-injection patterns such as 'ignore previous instructions'. A blocked query refuses here and goes no further.
srv.explain.source_coverage: A deterministic check that the contentful terms in the question (drug and condition names, clinical terms, qualifiers like 'children') appear in the retrieved sources; everyday words like 'email' or 'meeting' are not held against them. A term the index has but the passages lack gets one more search aimed at it, kept to the topic the question names. Catches questions about things the corpus never mentions, before generation.

view_ask.answers_come_only_from: Answers come only from approved sources, with a citation for every statement. When a question can’t be grounded, GroundCheckHealth refuses and sends it for review.

view_ehr.a_cds_hooks_request: A CDS Hooks request as an EHR would send it, for a draft order of Caloradine for a patient with reduced kidney function. Edit it and send it to see the cards.

view_embeddings.each_passage_projected_f: Each passage projected from its embedding to three dimensions with PCA, so similar passages sit together. Drag to rotate, hover a point. After you ask, the retrieved sources light up.
view_embeddings.how_passages_are_turned: How passages are turned into vectors and searched.
view_evaluation.every_release_runs_a: Every release runs a golden set of answerable and must-refuse questions, and adversarial probes.
view_local_ai.run_an_open_source: Run an open-source model on this machine. It drafts answers; the same checks still decide what is shown, and answers fall back to extractive mode if it isn’t available.
view_medicines.the_formulary_patient_che: The formulary patient checks use: allergies, interactions, and dose rules for age, weight, kidney and liver function, pregnancy and lab results.
view_models.trained_models_ready_to: Trained models, ready to use. Each abstains when it isn’t confident enough, or when an image doesn’t look like what it was trained on.
view_monitoring.alerts_from_live_use: Alerts from live use: refusals, response times, drift from the documents, overdue reviews, expiring documents and the audit trail. Prometheus can scrape
view_releases.every_change_to_what: Every change to what answers are grounded in is checked against the safety tests before it goes live. If something is wrong, go back to the previous release in one step.
view_review.every_refusal_and_flagged: Every refusal and flagged answer waits here for a clinician. Resolve a case as a test and the question is checked from then on.
view_training.train_an_image_classifier: Train an image classifier on a folder of your own images, on this machine’s GPU. The model is saved to the library, with its accuracy and the confidence below which it refuses to answer.
view_usage.questions_asked_what_was: Questions asked, what was answered and refused, how fast, and what needs review.
view_users.everyone_who_can_sign: Everyone who can sign in, their role, site and two-factor status.
viewer_keys.scroll_drag_the_slider: Scroll, drag the slider or use the arrow keys to move through slices. Page Up and Page Down jump ten.
